extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners, patent applicants and agents (KIPO procedures)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how examiners may perform ex‑officio amendments to patent documents and the procedures, eligibility, conduct and minutes requirements for preliminary examination interviews in Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "obvious mistakes" for ex-officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious mistakes in a specification, drawing(s) or an abstract (Article 66(2)) mean that a person skilled in the art should easily recognize the mistake and it can be easily anticipated how the documents are amended because the original intention of the applicant can be clearly understood in view of the specification, written argument and common general technical knowledge as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only where the original intention is clearly understandable (from specification, written argument and common general technical knowledge) may an examiner correct obvious mistakes ex‑officio.

rubrics_metrics.name: General matters amendable ex-officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters to be amended ex-officio include standard Korean terms, simple typos, an omitted word, inconsistency of drawing numerals and irregularities from which the original intention can be clearly found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples follow; if the intention of the applicant is not clearly understood, ex‑officio amendment is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misspelled word (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Misspelled words in violation of Korean grammar may be corrected ex‑officio (examples: 'Semiconducter' → 'Semiconductor'; 'Boared' → 'Board').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple misspellings are typical ex‑officio corrections when meaning is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing word obvious in grammar (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious omitted words that are clear in Korean grammar may be supplied ex‑officio (examples: 'signal transmitted ○ line' → 'signal transmitted to line'; 'linear ○tor' → 'linear motor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only where insertion is obvious to a skilled reader may the omission be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency in reference numerals (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inconsistencies between description and drawings in reference numerals may be corrected ex‑officio (example: description has Buffer (115) vs. Drawings Fig.2 Buffer (15)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend to make references consistent when the correct numeral is apparent from the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant writing (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Redundant repeated phrases may be deleted ex‑officio (example: 'The patent office, the patent office is' → 'The patent office is').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove obviously redundant text that does not affect meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error in simple explanation of drawing (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple mistakes in drawing explanations (e.g., misstated figure numbers or misspelled reference numerals in drawings) may be corrected ex‑officio (examples: wrong figure numbering; '3…Gear' vs '3…Motor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful not to introduce new technical matter; correct obvious labeling errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong indication of representative figure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the representative figure is obviously wrongly indicated considering the specification disclosure, the indication may be corrected ex‑officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should determine the obviously correct representative figure from the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency in title between description and application
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may amend the title in the description to correspond to the application; if the application title fails requirements, examiner may amend ex‑officio to a proper title and amend description title correspondingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use system corrections (e.g., 'correction ex officio' button) and ensure the title meets invention title requirements under the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing a deleted claim (antecedent corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a deleted claim is cited and only one antecedent claim exists, the citation may be amended ex‑officio to point to the remaining antecedent (examples provided converting references to the correct antecedent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust antecedent citations to the obvious remaining claim when citation would otherwise cite a deleted claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing claims where some cited claims were deleted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims that have not been deleted are cited in combination with deleted claims, citations may be amended ex‑officio to remove references to deleted claims (example: 'claim 1 or claim 2' where claim 2 is deleted → 'claim 1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make citation language coherent and reflect only existing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where dependent claim subject matter differs from citing claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dependent claim's subject matter differs from that of the claiming (antecedent) claim, the dependent language may be amended ex‑officio to restore consistent claim dependency (example converting a method dependency incorrectly referring to an apparatus into an apparatus dependency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure dependent claims properly refer to compatible claim types (e.g., apparatus vs method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining dependent claim into cited claim requires deletion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dependent claim is combined into the cited claim ex‑officio producing duplication, the dependent claim should then be deleted ex‑officio (example provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When consolidation makes a dependent claim redundant, delete the redundant claim to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical element referred by multiple terms (unify terminology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the same element is referred to by two or more different terms, examiner may correct to a single consistent term ex‑officio (example normalizing 'nuclear creation layer' → 'nucleation layer').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unify terms to avoid ambiguity when the identity is obvious from disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obvious wrong claim citation (correct target claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is obvious that a particular claim was cited incorrectly, examiner may correct to the obvious cited claim (example changing which claim is cited when context makes intent clear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only when the intended citation is obvious from the disclosure may it be fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated identical claim (delete duplicates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a literally identical claim is presented repeatedly, the duplicate claim may be deleted ex‑officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove literal duplicates to maintain proper claim set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cited claims not indicated as alternatives (correct conjunctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct non‑alternative citations to alternative form (examples: 'according to claims 1 and 2' → 'according to claim 1 or 2'; other corrections to indicate alternative claims properly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise alternative language (or, any one of) when claims are meant as alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for intended ex-officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner intending to amend ex‑officio shall notify the matters to be amended to the applicant with a certified copy of the decision to grant, describing in definite and specific manners which matters are to be amended and stating the reason to help the applicant decide to accept or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate exact paragraph/line numbers and give clear examples in the notice (example notice format provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant opposition to ex-officio amendment and legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant opposes acceptance (in whole or part) they may submit argument before patent fee payment; parts or all of the ex‑officio amendment where written argument is filed shall be deemed not to have been made, and the decision to grant shall be deemed revoked (except where only abstract amendments are deemed not made).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow applicant to select which ex‑officio amendments they accept; opposition triggers re‑examination for revoked grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination timeline after non-acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant files written argument opposing ex‑officio amendment (other than abstract amendments), the examiner shall re‑examine the application within 1 month from transmission of the written argument (Regulation 26(2)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re‑examination should be carried out promptly and within prescribed timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome when re-examination finds no grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If re‑examination cannot find grounds for rejection, the examiner shall grant a patent or utility model registration; ex‑officio amendment originally opposed shall not be re‑applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not re‑amend the matters the applicant originally opposed if re‑examination cleared them (Regulation 26(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome when re-examination finds grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If re‑examination finds grounds for rejection, the examiner shall notify the grounds to the applicant; even if the ground had been notified before ex‑officio amendment, the notification shall be issued again, but where the ground is relevant to an opposed ex‑officio amendment already notified, examiner may decide to reject without further notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural rules on re‑notification and when direct rejection is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments before ex-officio shall not be refused entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made by the applicant before ex‑officio amendment shall not be refused entry; this reduces unpredictability for applicants who thought grounds had been overcome when a decision to grant was made (Article 51(1)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect applicant‑filed amendments that predate ex‑officio changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change claim scope by ex-officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Care should be taken that the scope of the claims should not be changed by ex‑officio amendment; if there is any possibility that terms may be construed differently, ex‑officio amendment should not be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about claim scope effects, refrain from ex‑officio changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification practice combining ex-officio amendment and grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When grounds for rejection are notified to an applicant, matters for ex‑officio amendment should be notified all together so the applicant may amend accordingly; obvious errors failing description requirements shall be notified as grounds for rejection, while simple typos shall be notified as advice of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between advice (typos) and formal grounds (description deficiencies) in communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid introducing new matter in ex-officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should be careful not to add new matters not disclosed in the original description or drawings by amendment ex‑officio; in particular avoid introducing unintended new technical subject‑matter in drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all corrections are supported by the original filing; do not expand disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: do not amend if applicant's intention is unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if obviously wrong, if the applicant’s intention is not clearly understood from specification and written arguments, ex‑officio amendment is not permitted (example: ambiguous antecedent claim among plural antecedents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear evidence of applicant intent before correcting ambiguous matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial non-acceptance: effect on other ex-officio amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant does not accept parts of ex‑officio amendment, those parts are deemed not to have been made, but other parts remain; care must be taken that remaining parts are not then treated as grounds for rejection, and ensure remaining parts are reflected in final amendment or re‑applied as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm which parts remain in final documents post re‑examination and avoid mis‑notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct claim numbering after ex-officio deletions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number of claims changes because the examiner deletes claims ex‑officio (e.g., duplicate literal claims), the number of claims shall be corrected ex‑officio on the Patent Net interface for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update claim numbering in the electronic system to match the amended claim set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of main drawing by examiner ex-officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant did not or wrongly established a main drawing that explains claimed subject matter, the examiner can replace the main drawing ex‑officio with another that better explains the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ex‑officio drawing replacement sparingly and only where it clarifies the claimed subject matter without adding new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of preliminary examination (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary examination promotes accurate examination and early allowance by sharing opinions between examiner and applicant through an interview before substantive examination, allowing consultation on potential grounds for rejection and amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the interview to facilitate rapid voluntary amendment and accurate substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications eligible for preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary examination can be carried out for an application for which an examiner has determined to expedite examination and which falls within a classification requiring higher than average difficulty; for PPH cases, preliminary examination is conducted for those decided to be expedited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility centers on expedited status and higher difficulty classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or an agent is allowed to request preliminary examination (via Patent‑Ro website).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be filed through the specified online form and include required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may participate in the interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must have responsibility to respond, including the applicant (or corporate representative), an agent, or a subagent authorized to participate; inventors may participate; for applications handled by an assistant examiner, the supervising examiner must participate with the assistant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agent exists, the agent should participate to make the interview effective; identity verification may be required for unpublished applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of preliminary examination interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Any matter can be discussed: applicant explains technical content and differences with prior art; examiner explains results of preliminary review on patentability and deficiencies; parties discuss how to amend claims to resolve grounds for rejection and secure appropriate scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview aims to facilitate amendment and understanding; avoid using interview as venue for matters outside scope (progress queries etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request timing and scheduling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary examination must be requested within 14 days from date of sending notice of decision on expedited examination; applicant should present 3 desired interview dates within 3–6 weeks from request, and include petitioner info, application number, desired dates, participants and contact number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If office action issued before request, interview is not necessary; requests filed via Patent‑Ro (Request for application → Request for preliminary examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner decision on request timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request, the examiner shall decide to accept or reject the preliminary examination request through Patent Net within 7 days from the request date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision considers difficulty, expedited status, participants, proposed dates and other factors; if prior art search required, interview may be scheduled later to allow preview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific requirements to decide preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements include: (①) application having high level of difficulty; (②) application decided for expedited examination (including PPH cases where examiner decides to expedite); (③) request filed within timing limits; (④) proper interview participants (applicant, agent, inventor, authorized person); (⑤) desired interview dates within 3–6 weeks; (⑥) absence of inappropriate reasons (e.g., too broad claim scope for interview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requirements should be satisfied, but examiner may suggest corrections or accept ex‑officio if possible after consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and scheduling practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner accepts requests for applications meeting requirements, selects an interview date from the applicant’s proposed dates, and if prior art search is required, schedules interview about a month later to allow preview; examiner may accept ex‑officio if issues can be resolved through discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the desired dates fit, examiner may coordinate by phone; preview and prior art search improve interview effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of request for preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may return the request if it does not meet requirements and cannot be corrected via consultation; applicant may reapply after resolving grounds within the 14‑day request period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returning does not bar reapplication within the allowed request window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay or cancellation of interview
rubrics_metrics.description: If the interview cannot be held due to applicant‑caused inevitable grounds, examiner gives one more chance to reschedule (within 3–6 weeks); if grounds are unacceptable, the interview can be canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit rescheduling opportunities to preserve schedule integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner preparation for interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Before interview, examiner shall read the claimed invention, review patentability requirements and specification deficiencies comprehensively to an extent comparable to substantive examination, prepare documents, prior art search results, Minutes and Additional paper for the minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State preview results in minutes to explain to applicant; ensure examiner is ready to explain grounds and suggestions clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant identification and security in interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall identify each participant before the interview (use ID for unpublished applications); if participant refuses process, the interview may be limited or halted; if participant is different from applicant who applied, interview can be halted, delayed or limited for security and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interviews occur in secure buildings, check IDs; protect unpublished application confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted interview topics — applicant technical explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may explain complicated or advanced technical contents directly, using prototypes or multimedia (photo, video); examiner may request presentation materials in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials help examiner understanding; examiner may require materials ahead of time for preview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted interview topics — applicant preliminary amendment suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant can explain suggested preliminary amendments submitted in advance; examiner may give opinion on suggestions within allowed scope to help rapid and accurate examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions and voluntary amendments should be submitted at least 14 days before interview; examiner may not give opinions on late submissions if preview is already finished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted interview topics — comparison with prior art and argument for patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may explain claimed invention by comparing with prior art (submitted search results) and argue differences and patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior art search results to frame comparative technical arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted interview topics — examiner explains grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners shall explain the result of their preliminary review on patentability and deficiencies in the specification and, if appropriate, actively suggest ways to resolve grounds for rejection during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral explanation in the interview is sufficient; examiner should prepare an opinion on grounds in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted interview topics — discussion on possible amendment and non-binding nature of suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant and examiner shall consult on possible amendments to resolve grounds and secure appropriate scope; examiner's suggestions have no legal binding force and the final decision on amendment is the applicant's responsibility; suggestions may change based on new prior art or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must not order or lead the applicant to follow suggestions and should explicitly state lack of binding force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes of interview — required content and signing
rubrics_metrics.description: After interview, applicant and examiner shall prepare and sign minutes; minutes shall be uploaded to Patent Net and may be distributed to applicant. Minutes must state interview date, place, application number, title, participant names, examiner’s opinion on grounds for rejection, suggestion of amendment discussed, and applicant’s arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed minutes become part of examination history and should include paragraph/line references for clarity; upload promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes — stating opinion on grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion on grounds for rejection should reflect results of review of patentability and specification deficiencies and applicant responses; examiner may prepare this in advance but should orally explain during the interview; minutes need only state purpose of grounds for rejection as reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include applicant’s arguments in response; example table format provided in guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes — stating suggestion of amendment discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner's suggestion of amendment was discussed and any result reached (agreement or language of amendment), the result of discussion shall be recorded in the minutes as an examination record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record agreed language or amendment outcomes to create a clear examination trail.
